data.name: Clotilda
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'clotus' meaning mud, and 'tilda' meaning glory. The name Clotilda was borne by a saint and martyr in the 5th century. She was a Frankish princess who converted to Christianity and was executed for her faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents the spiritual journey from the mundane to the divine.

in_hebrew.name: כלותילדה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: כלותילדה (Clotilda) - פירוש: בת המלך, גבורה, נשמה, נפרד. נצרות: נטען כי הכלפה, מלכת הפרנקים, נולדה סביב 470 CE. כלותילדה היא שם-משפחה נרדף, נפוץ באירופה. שם-העם בצרפת, (Clotilde) - שם-פאם כלפה.

in_greek.name: Κλοτίλδη
in_greek.long_meaning: Κλοτίλδη - συνώνυμο: παῖς βασιλέως, θυμαία, ψυχή, διαχωρισμένη. Χριστιανισμός: υποστηρίζεται ότι η Χλοθilde, βασίλισσα των Φράγκων, γεννήθηκε γύρω στο 470 μ.Χ. Η Κλοτίλδη είναι ένα κοινό επώνυμο, περιβαλλοντικό σε Ευρώπη. Ονοματεπώνυμο Κλοτίλδη (ή Κλοτίλδη) - ονοματεπώνυμο.

in_latin.name: Clotilda
in_latin.long_meaning: Clotilda - significatio: filia regis, fortitudo, anima, disposita. Christianitas: Clotilda, regina Francorum, nata circa annum 470. Clotilda nomen- familiae commune, frequentantur in Europa. Nomen- persona Clotilda (aut Clotilda) - nomen- persona.

in_english.name: Clotilda
in_english.meaning: daughter of the king, strength, soul, separated
in_english.long_meaning: Clotilda - meaning: daughter of the king, strength, soul, separated. Christianity: Clotilda, queen of the Franks, born circa 470 AD. Clotilda is a common surname, widespread in Europe. Clotilda as a given name (or Clotilda) - given name.

saint_reference.note: Saint Clotilda of France (c. 475-545 AD) is a saint in the Catholic Church. She is the wife of King Clovis I of the Franks and the mother of King Childebert I. She is revered for her piety and her role in the conversion of her husband to Christianity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Clotilda holds a significant place in the history of early Christianity in Europe. Clotilda, a Frankish princess, is remembered for her greatest act of faith – converting to Christianity and spreading its teachings despite the daunting risks. Her story is a testament to the power of faith and courage in the face of adversity, and her name became synonymous with religious conversion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Clotilda signifies the transformative power of faith. Just as mud can be molded and shaped, Clotilda, through her faith, transformed her life and her culture. The name also holds deeper spiritual meaning, representing the idea that even the mundane and ordinary, such as mud, can reveal something beautiful and profound in God's design. Furthermore, Clotilda is a reminder of the ultimate sacrifice that some Christians made to spread the word of God, inspiring future generations to continue sharing their faith.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Clotilda was a Frankish queen who married Clovis I in 493 AD. The name Clotilda carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Clotilda continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Clotilda from Athens, Greece embodies the meaning of Clotilda - "Glory in the mud". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Clotilda: Dedicated to St. Clotilde, a Frankish queen who converted to Christianity and influenced her husband, King Chilperic, to do the same. Her name means "famous in war" but also symbolizes her victory in converting her husband and people to the Christian faith.
